substeps.caption: A 250 mL jar of powder goes into the printed nest.
The LX500c prints its label: sample ID, alloy, mass, date and a QR code. The AP380 takes such labels die-cut on a roll.
The jar goes into the AP380, lying down on its rollers; the pressure arm comes down.
One press of the foot switch: the rollers turn the jar once and the label wraps on.
The pressure arm lifts. Out, and into a clear liner bag, standing in front of the H-190 impulse sealer.
The bag's mouth goes across the jaw, and the sealer closes on it: a 12 in seal.
Into the foam insert's cut-out, lying down.
The ZD621 prints the 4 x 6 in shipping label, and it goes on the lid. Whether the box needs dangerous-goods marks depends on a test, not on the alloy's name.
